results.title: Can People See Your Bookmarks on X? (2026) | ContextBolt
results.content:
## The honest take on who can see your X bookmarks

Strip it back and the situation is simple. Nobody can see your bookmarks on X. They are genuinely private, more private than likes, more private than your follows, and the author never knows you saved their post. The public count is a total with no names attached, and the recurring “bookmarks are going public” rumor is a hoax that has never come true. [...] ## Can people see your bookmarks on X?

No. This is one of the few questions on X with a clean, documented answer. The X Help Center page on bookmarks says it plainly: bookmarks are private and only viewable to you within your X account.

That has been true since bookmarks launched in 2018, and it has stayed true under X’s current ownership. Bookmarks were built as a quiet, personal save feature, the opposite of a like. A like is a public signal. A bookmark is a private note to yourself. [...] Quick answer

 No, nobody can see your bookmarks on X. Not followers, not accounts you follow, not the post’s author.
 Bookmarks are not public. X’s Help Center states they are only viewable to you inside your own account.
 The author gets no notification when you save their post, and there is no list of who bookmarked it.
 The one public signal is a total count. Each post shows how many times it was saved, but never by whom.
 Bookmark folders are private too. X Premium changes what you can organize, not who can look.
 Privacy ends when you export. Move your saves off X and it depends on where the new tool stores them.

## The Tool That Finally Worked: Circleboom Twitter

This part surprised me — there is a safe way to export bookmarks, but it’s not through Twitter’s interface. It’s through Circleboom Twitter, one of the few platforms that’s actually an official X/Twitter partner.

And this “official partner” detail matters.  
A lot.

It means:

That’s exactly the kind of reassurance I needed before giving any tool access to my bookmarks.

So I used it.  
And honestly? It solved the problem instantly.

How?

You should follow these steps:

Step #1: Visit the Circleboom Twitter website and sign in using your account credentials.

Circleboom is an official X Enterprise partner! So, your account and all the data you have is safe and secure with us!

Press enter or click to view image in full size [...] Press enter or click to view image in full size

Step #2: Find your “Bookmarks”.

Hover on “My Tweets & Lists” and click on “Delete Bookmarks” from the menu on the left.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Step #3: Check the box next to each bookmarked tweet that you want to export, or you can “Select All” to download all of them.

Then click on the “Export” button at the top right.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Click on the blue button, and your selected bookmarked tweets will be downloaded soon.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Once the bookmarks are exported, they will be saved in a spreadsheet format (CSV or Excel file). The file contains detailed tweet information.

## What Happened When I Exported My Bookmarks [...] ## Why This Matters More Than It Seems

Losing a few bookmarks didn’t feel like a big deal at first.  
But the more I thought about it, the more I realized how fragile our saved digital content really is.

Bookmarks disappear silently.  
Creators delete tweets without warning.  
Accounts go private.  
Threads get edited or removed.

If you use Twitter for learning, research, content ideas, or work, you’re relying on something that can vanish at any time.

Exporting your bookmarks gives you:

It turns “I hope this tweet is still there next week” into “I own this now.”

## If You’re Thinking About Exporting Yours…

My advice?  
Do it before you need to.

If I had waited just a little longer, I would’ve lost even more saved content without realizing it.
